page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-32 is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Vector extensions are limited to standard AVX without AVX-512 or AMX support, while dedicated cryptographic acceleration is supplied via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. The configuration contains no local storage and does not include GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive throughput across integer, memory, and specialized computation tasks. The instance delivers top-tier memory performance, with a PassMark memory score of 3062.11 placing it in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth registers at 129.76 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 65.71 GB/sec for writes. Computational evaluation shows strong single-core stress-ng performance at 2903.79 (top 25%) and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 14686.0. Hardware-assisted cryptography provides strong results, reaching 37415.59 in PassMark CPU encryption tests. For CPU-based machine learning inference, the instance achieves top-tier results in small model text generation (357.74 tokens/sec) and strong performance on medium 7B parameter models (28.17 tokens/sec), though larger 70B parameter prompt processing falls into the bottom 25% due to architectural scaling limits.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires external persistent disks for data persistence, which shifts primary storage I/O performance characteristics to network-attached block volumes. Because memory bandwidth and single-core frequency are strong, the instance provides efficient resource utilization for compute workloads that require high throughput without incurring the cost overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators.

Given its high core count, top-tier memory scores, and robust cryptographic handling, GCP c2d-standard-32 is appropriate for web serving, continuous integration builds, distributed caching systems like Redis, image processing, and medium-scale CPU inference pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-32 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 16-core, 32-thread AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs, 128 GB of RAM (4 GB per vCPU), and a 32 MB L3 cache, with no local storage or attached GPUs. Supported CPU extensions include AVX, VAES, and SHA_NI. The instance excels in memory-intensive benchmarks, recording a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3062.11 and 129.76 GB/sec uncached large-block read bandwidth. Cryptographic execution and single-core stress-ng benchmarks place in the top 25%, alongside strong lightweight LLM text generation metrics. While lack of integrated NVMe drives necessitates external network storage, its robust computational and memory efficiency makes it well-matched for compilation, web serving, in-memory caching, and medium-scale batch workloads.
